I now have the full picture. Here's the state of §5 ("Prevent future leaks"):

| Sub-item | Status |
|---|---|
| Harden `.gitignore` (`.env*`, `*.sql.gz`, `*.ibd`, `*.frm`, datadirs) | ✅ Already on main (root + app) — minor dedupe possible |
| CI secret scanning (gitleaks) | ✅ Already on main (`security-scan.yml` → "Secret Scan" job) |
| `.gitleaks.toml` config + allowlists | ✅ Already on main |
| **Pre-commit** gitleaks/git-secrets hook | ❌ Missing (`.git/hooks` empty, no shared config) |

| **Replace data dumps with synthetic seeder** | ⚠️ Partial — see below |

On the dumps: there are **two**, with very different coupling:
- `database/dev/familyfund_dev_data.sql` — **still tracked**, contains real PII (1 gmail + 9 bcrypt hashes). It's gitignored but never untracked. **Nothing loads it** — only the security docs reference it; the canonical dev-load is `prod-to-dev.sh` (uses gitignored prod dumps). Safe to untrack now.
- `app1/family-fund-app/database/test/test-baseline.sql.gz` (275 KB, ~62 emails) — **load-bearing**: CI `tests.yml` and `testpool.sh` both restore the whole suite from it. Replacing it with a synthetic seeder is an epic that touches all 1791 tests.

That last point is the one real fork in scope, so let me confirm direction before I build.
